CountCancelled.description:
A count on this request was cancelled by the server before it finished (IMGMGR-176).

The count path answers population questions over the whole library — the facet chips, a
grouped grid's ``total``, the selection size — and those are the statements a backup
window or an operator ``pg_cancel_backend`` cancels first. Postgres reports the cancel as
SQLSTATE ``57014``, which reaches the app WRAPPED as ``sqlalchemy.exc.DBAPIError``; left
unhandled it surfaced as a bare 500, which tells a client the server is broken when the
truth is that it is busy and the identical request will work shortly.

So: 503 with this code and a ``Retry-After`` beside it, exactly as
:class:`StackEditBusy` answers a folder lock it could not take. Never a partial body and
never a null ``total`` — a count that could not be taken is not a count of zero.
CountCancelled.title: CountCancelled

CountCancelledError.description:
The ``count_cancelled`` 503 body as it goes on the wire.

FastAPI wraps an ``HTTPException`` detail in ``{"detail": ...}``, so the declared shape
carries that envelope — the :class:`StackEditBusyError` idiom, for the same reason.
CountCancelledError.title: CountCancelledError

DateBucket.description:
One Zurich calendar day in the current scope, and how to jump to it.

``cursor`` is a SEEK token, not a filter: it positions the keyset at the start of that
day so the grid can reset its window there while still holding one continuous result
set. A date filter would hide everything before the day instead of scrolling to it.
DateBucket.title: DateBucket

DownloadEstimate.description:
What "download everything I am looking at" would cost, asked BEFORE it starts.

Its own route and its own model rather than a mode of the download itself: one operation
that answered either JSON or a zip under one 200 would generate a client type that is
neither. The caps travel with the answer so the UI can explain the refusal it is about
to get instead of discovering it as a 413, and ``capped`` is a report — this endpoint
never refuses.

``total_bytes`` is the indexed size of the files that would be packed, so it is the same
number the cap is compared against. The archive that arrives can differ by whatever the
disk did since the last scan; the archive's own MANIFEST records what it actually holds.
DownloadEstimate.title: DownloadEstimate

DownloadVariant.description:
One content choice the current selection ACTUALLY holds, measured.

The dialog offers what is there rather than a fixed pair, so a variant with no members in
this selection is ABSENT from the list rather than present with a zero: an option that
packs nothing is a download that arrives empty. That absence is also why the caps travel
per variant — originals may be over the ceiling while the masters of the same filter are
not, and the reader has to be told which of the offers they can actually take.
DownloadVariant.title: DownloadVariant

FolderSummary.description:
One CANONICAL folder's shoot-summary row (WP7 P4, IMGMGR-110) — the folder of P1's
canonical image identity, never a raw physical folder (fold item 1). Distinct from
``FolderNode``: that response's counts are PHYSICAL per-tier counts and its meaning is
untouched by this phase (fold item 2); every count here is a LOGICAL, canonical-image
count, deduplicated across a mirrored tier pair.
FolderSummary.title: FolderSummary

FolderSyncCounts.description:
Write-back sync-status tally over images in this folder that carry a Mark row
(WP7 P3, IMGMGR-111) — never the folder's full ``image_count``: an unmarked
photograph was never eligible for write-back and sits outside this tally entirely.
FolderSyncCounts.title: FolderSyncCounts

FolderSyncStatusOut.description:
``latest`` is the newest request whose scope COVERS the folder (the folder's own, or a
whole-library one); ``cannot_travel`` counts the ELIGIBLE marked non-RAW targets.
FolderSyncStatusOut.title: FolderSyncStatusOut

GroupHeader.description:
One bucket of ``GET /api/image-groups`` — every selected image belongs to exactly one
of these, including the explicit Unknown bucket (``key=None``) for absent metadata.
GroupHeader.title: GroupHeader

HealthResponse.description: Liveness. Deliberately carries no ``db`` field — see ``health()``.
HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

ImageFacets.description:
Counts for each filter chip, computed with the OTHER filters applied.

Drill-down semantics: the number beside "rating >= 4" is what you would get by clicking
it, so the rating filter itself is excluded from its own count while every other active
filter still applies.
ImageFacets.title: ImageFacets

ImageGroups.description:
Group aggregates over the current browse filters (WP7 P7, IMGMGR-140/141) — headers
with counts for a ``group_by`` the grid can page (``group_by`` on ``/api/images``/
``/api/images/{id}/neighbours``) without ever aggregating or reordering rows itself.

``sum(headers[].count) == total``, including Unknown — this endpoint never excludes
undated/unlocated/unattributed images the way ``/api/dates`` does, because a header
count that could not sum to ``total`` would be a group the grid could not fully page.
``total`` is the same number ``/api/facets`` reports under identical filters (both read
the distinct-image-id count over the identical joined/filtered query).
ImageGroups.title: ImageGroups

ImageLookRequest.description:
``PUT /api/images/{image_id}/look`` (P7, IMGMGR-537): save a look on a photograph.

``strength`` is strict: a fractional number, a string or a boolean is a malformed
request (``invalid_request``), never coerced. A ``look_id`` outside the catalogue is the
handler's own ``unknown_look``.
ImageLookRequest.title: ImageLookRequest

ImageLookView.description:
The saved look on a photograph (P7, IMGMGR-537): which catalogue look, how strong.

``strength`` is a percentage, 0..200 (100 = the look as authored). ``updated_at`` is the
mutation time of the last write — concurrent writes are last-write-wins and the value
carries no monotonicity promise across them.
ImageLookView.title: ImageLookView

LightroomMeta.description:
Read-only truth from the XMP sidecar. Never merged with the app's own marks.

``sidecar_present`` is a first-class field because absence is data: no sidecar means
Lightroom has never touched the image, which is a different statement from rating 0.
LightroomMeta.title: LightroomMeta

LookList.description:
Every look the server can currently apply, in curated manifest order.

A look whose vendored asset failed its integrity check is ABSENT rather than flagged:
the list answers "what can be applied", and an unreadable LUT cannot. The shortfall is
visible by counting, and the reason is in the log (``looks_asset_invalid``).
LookList.title: LookList

LookRefusal.description:
Why a looked proxy request was refused, coded — the WP17 envelope for a new operation.

The operation ``GET /api/images/{image_id}/proxy/{tier}/look/{look_id}`` is NEW, so
declaring this model as its 422 in place of FastAPI's ``HTTPValidationError`` is additive
(a whole new endpoint is never a breach under ``app.openapi_contract``) — which is what
makes IMGMGR-380's "coded 422 per the WP17 envelope" reachable without a second breaking
recut. It is only true because BOTH 422 producers on the route arrive in this envelope:
the handler's ``unknown_look`` and the validation handler's ``invalid_request``.
LookRefusal.title: LookRefusal

LookRefusalError.description: The coded 422 body as it goes on the wire — the :class:`StackEditRefusalError` idiom.
LookRefusalError.title: LookRefusalError

LookSummary.description:
One catalogued look (WP24 P0, IMGMGR-380) — a display-time colour transform, never
library state and never anything written to a photograph.

The published fields are the catalogue's descriptive half plus ``version``. The asset
filename and its digest stay server-side: the first is a filesystem-shaped field this
module's R-B6 rule keeps off the wire, and the second answers a question ("are the
shipped bytes intact") the server has already answered by the time it publishes a look
at all. ``version`` (IMGMGR-642) is the first twelve hex of that digest, but it is not
the integrity digest: it is the identity a client saves a look against, sent back as
``ImageLookRequest.look_version``. R-B6 concerns path-shaped fields only.

``licence`` is ONE line that must carry the whole record, including a split one. Nine of
the twelve looks have a LUT-data licence that is UNRESOLVED and a mirror-repository
licence (GPL-3.0) that covers only that repository's packaging; the manifest states both
halves in this single string and this model copies it verbatim. Narrowing it to the
resolved half would publish settled terms where there are none, which is exactly what
``tests/test_looks_catalogue.py`` and ``tests/test_api_looks.py`` exist to prevent.
LookSummary.title: LookSummary

LookVersionConflict.description:
Why a saved-look write refused (IMGMGR-642): the client chose the look at a version
the catalogue no longer serves. A NEW model rather than a new ``LookRefusalCode`` value:
a response enum may not change under ``app.openapi_contract``. Nothing was written.
LookVersionConflict.title: LookVersionConflict

LookVersionConflictError.description: The 409 body as it goes on the wire — the :class:`SyncConflictError` idiom.
LookVersionConflictError.title: LookVersionConflictError

MaintenanceBusy.description:
Why ``POST /api/reindex`` refused, and which run is in the way.

The refusal carries the ACTIVE run rather than a bare message so the UI can follow the
work that is already going instead of guessing at it — that is the whole reason the
endpoint refuses rather than queueing a successor.
MaintenanceBusy.title: MaintenanceBusy

MaintenanceBusyError.description:
The 409 body as it goes on the wire.

FastAPI wraps an ``HTTPException`` detail in ``{"detail": ...}``, so the declared shape
has to carry that envelope or the generated client would type the refusal one level too
shallow. This model exists to be DECLARED, not returned: the handler raises the
exception, and this says what the exception becomes.
MaintenanceBusyError.title: MaintenanceBusyError

MaintenanceStatus.description:
What the loop is doing, and whether it can do anything at all.

``tier_mounted`` is three-valued on purpose: null is "not evaluated yet", which is not
the same statement as "the tier is gone" — the banner must be able to say "unknown".
MaintenanceStatus.title: MaintenanceStatus

MarkPrecondition.description:
One submitted image id's expected current revision (IMGMGR-117 fold item 1).

Optional on every mark-mutating request, and additive FOREVER: a request that omits
``preconditions`` entirely is unconditional, exactly as before this field existed, and
no future phase may make it mandatory (that would be a breaking request change against
IMGMGR-117's own acceptance contract).
MarkPrecondition.title: MarkPrecondition

MarkRevision.description:
The revision an image's logical mark carries AFTER a mutation — returned for every
submitted id, including one whose write was idempotent (applied nothing). Mirrored
aliases submitted together carry the same value, because they share one mark row.
MarkRevision.title: MarkRevision

MarkStateRequest.description: Set-shaped by design (spec C-3): one image is a set of one.

preconditions.description: optional; when present must exactly cover the deduplicated image_ids (malformed or partial coverage is 422); a stale revision refuses the whole request with 409 stale_mark_revision and applies nothing
preconditions.title: Preconditions

MarkStateRequest.title: MarkStateRequest

MarkView.description: The app's own writable state. One tri-state, never two toggles.
MarkView.title: MarkView

MarksApplied.description: ``applied`` counts images whose state ACTUALLY changed — an idempotent re-write is 0.
MarksApplied.title: MarksApplied

MarksExport.description:
The marked set as filename stems, for pasting into Lightroom's Library filter.

``count`` is the number of stems IN THIS RESPONSE, so it still describes the payload
when ``truncated`` is true — a count that reported the uncapped total would make the
list look complete when it is not.
MarksExport.title: MarksExport

NativeTokenOut.description:
The one shape a device ever receives a token in — exchange and renewal both answer
with this, so a client parses a renewal with the same decoder it parsed its first
token with (p1-spec-rev2.md "Exchange/renew response").
NativeTokenOut.title: NativeTokenOut

ProxyState.description: One tier of one image: what the client may do about it right now.
ProxyState.title: ProxyState

RenditionChip.description: A Lightroom-rendered artifact this image has. Filename only — never its path.
RenditionChip.title: RenditionChip

RunCounters.description:
What a run did, as a typed projection of the executor's own counters.

Deliberately not the raw blob. The executor records free-form maps keyed by category and
by failure reason, and the database keeps all of it for whoever is debugging a run — but
an API field typed ``dict[str, Any]`` is a hole in every rule about what this API may
emit: a future counter carrying a path would reach the browser with nothing to stop it,
and no field-level guard could see it coming. Only these numbers cross the wire.
RunCounters.title: RunCounters

RunProgress.description:
Live progress on a STILL-RUNNING run (WP7 P8, IMGMGR-157) — additive: present only
while the executor has published at least one bounded-cadence update for this run, never
on a finished one (``finish_run`` overwrites ``counters`` wholesale with the lane's final
numbers, which carry no ``progress`` key at all). Raw counts, not a pre-divided
percentage — the one arithmetic step (``completed / total``) is cheap enough that
keeping it in one place (the frontend) beats two implementations agreeing by convention.
RunProgress.title: RunProgress

SelectionItem.description:
One image the whole-result selection matched, with its mark AS OF this read.

The mark snapshot is mandatory (P7 rev2 premise-gate blocker 2): an ids-only response
would force the client to fetch a detail per unloaded id (an unbounded fan-out through
the expensive detail/availability path) or fabricate ``"none"`` as an unloaded row's
prior state — both closed by carrying the snapshot the client's Undo needs directly.
SelectionItem.title: SelectionItem

SelectionResponse.description:
``GET /api/images/selection`` — every id the current browse filters match, over the
cap boundary (WP7 P7, IMGMGR-140/141).

``total`` is always the TRUE count, capped or not — the UI's over-cap copy names it. Below
or at ``cap`` (inclusive: exactly ``cap`` succeeds), ``items`` holds one entry per matched
image, deterministic by image id. Over ``cap``, ``over_cap`` is ``true`` and ``items`` is
empty — never a silently actionable prefix a client could mistake for the whole match.
SelectionResponse.title: SelectionResponse

StackAbsorbRequest.description:
Take these LOOSE photographs into the scene — the eject's inverse (IMGMGR-289).

Every other editor starts from a membership and merge starts from two scenes, so a
photograph belonging to no scene could never join one. This starts from the stream.

The ids are exact PHYSICAL ``Image.id``s, the same identity every other topology verb
names, and nothing on this route resolves a canonical twin: an archive photograph's local
mirror is a different row here, as it is to merge, eject, split and extract.

A duplicate id names ONE photograph. The set is deduplicated before anything is checked or
written, and the DEDUPED count is the number the write's rowcount is held against — so a
body that named the same photograph twice is not read as an edit that half-failed.
StackAbsorbRequest.title: StackAbsorbRequest

StackBrowseImageRow.description: A loose photo in the stack-mode stream: one image, exactly as flat browse renders it.
StackBrowseImageRow.title: StackBrowseImageRow

StackBrowsePage.description:
One page of DISPLAY ROWS: loose photos and collapsed scenes in one capture order.

``limit`` counts display rows, not photographs — a page of 100 may stand for thousands of
frames. Chronological only in v0.11: a stack has ONE stored anchor, and an anchor per sort
key would be a redesign (plan Decision 1).
StackBrowsePage.title: StackBrowsePage

StackBrowseStackRow.description:
A collapsed scene: one card standing for every member.

``representative`` is a whole ``ImageSummary`` rather than an id because the card draws a
real tile — a cover rendition, an aspect ratio, a mark state. Its ``id`` is therefore ON
the wire and is DISPLAY-ONLY: the transport cannot conceal it (any rendition URL embeds an
image id), so the no-hidden-member-writes invariant is enforced at the CLIENT actionability
boundary (Phase 3), not by pretending the id is absent.

``member_count`` and ``has_pick`` aggregate over ALL members, filtered or not — the badges
describe the scene. ``matched_count`` is the other question: how many members the ACTIVE
browse filters match, which is what makes §F(4) ("filtering keeps the stack as the display
unit") legible rather than silently misleading.

``picked_count`` (IMGMGR-239) is the badge ``has_pick`` could not be. A boolean makes a scene
with one pick and a scene with nine look identical on a card, and the client cannot count them
itself: a collapsed scene's members are never loaded. It is a badge, so it counts ALL members
like the two beside it, never the matching ones — and it counts the CURRENT pick state, so an
un-pick takes a photograph back out of it.

``edited_count`` (IMGMGR-263) is the card's ``[✎n]``: how many members Lightroom has
exported a master for, the same ``has_edit`` bit a single tile shows as a pencil. It is a
badge like the two above it, so it counts ALL members and not the matching ones, and it is
the only way a card can carry the fact at all — a collapsed scene's membership never
reaches the client, so a client that wanted to say "2 edited" would have to open the scene
to find out.

``anchor_taken_at`` is the scene's STORED place in capture order, and it is on the wire
because ``representative.captured_at`` cannot answer the same question. The cover is derived
at read time (plan Decision 4) and moves the moment a member is picked, so a client that
sectioned the stream by the cover's timestamp would watch a scene jump from one day heading
to another on a mark — and a scene spanning midnight would sit under whichever day its cover
happened to belong to. The anchor moves only on an explicit split/merge/eject. ``None`` for a
scene whose members carry no capture time at all, which sorts in the NULL block exactly as a
loose photograph without one does.
StackBrowseStackRow.title: StackBrowseStackRow

StackEditBusy.description:
Why a stack edit refused before it started, and nothing about the stack's state.

A maintenance lane holds the folder while it derives or repairs anchors, and the request
role's short ``lock_timeout`` is what stops an editor waiting behind it with a pooled
connection. So the refusal is 503 and never 409: the request conflicts with nothing, the
server simply could not start yet, and the ``Retry-After`` header beside this body names
when it is worth asking again.
StackEditBusy.title: StackEditBusy

StackEditBusyError.description:
The 503 body as it goes on the wire (IMGMGR-278).

FastAPI wraps an ``HTTPException`` detail in ``{"detail": ...}``, so the declared shape has
to carry that envelope or a generated client would type the refusal one level too shallow.
Like :class:`MaintenanceBusyError` and :class:`StaleMarkRevisionError`, which it mirrors, it
exists to be DECLARED and not returned: ``app.api.stacks._lock_folder_or_busy`` raises the
exception and this says what the exception becomes. ``tests/test_api_stack_edit.py``
validates the LIVE body against it rather than trusting the declaration.
StackEditBusyError.title: StackEditBusyError

StackEditRefusal.description:
Why a stack edit was refused as unacceptable, coded (IMGMGR-288).

The stack editors have answered coded 422s since IMGMGR-278 — ``{"code": …, "message": …}``
inside FastAPI's ``detail`` envelope — while the published contract said
``HTTPValidationError`` for all of them, so every generated client typed a refusal it can
act on as a validation error it cannot. This model is that shipped body, said out loud;
the wire shape does not change.

The two refusals that were NOT coded are brought into it rather than left beside it, so the
declaration is true for every 422 these routes can emit: a merge of fewer than two distinct
scenes is ``too_few_stacks`` (it was a plain string), and a malformed request body is
``invalid_request`` (it was FastAPI's ``HTTPValidationError``, mapped by the route-scoped
handler in ``app.main``). One declaration that covers every case beats a union a Swift
generator turns into an unreachable branch.
StackEditRefusal.title: StackEditRefusal

StackEditRefusalError.description: The coded 422 body as it goes on the wire — the :class:`StackEditBusyError` idiom.
StackEditRefusalError.title: StackEditRefusalError

StackEditResult.description:
What an edit did, in ids — never a rendered row.

Deliberately not the refreshed cards: a mutation carries no browse filters, so any
``matched_count`` it invented would be computed in a filter context the caller never
asked for. The caller re-reads each surviving stack through ``GET /api/stacks/{id}`` with
its OWN active filters, which is the same live-refresh transport a mark write already uses.
StackEditResult.title: StackEditResult

StackExtractConflict.description:
Why an extraction refused because the scene is not in the state it was asked about.

Both codes describe the same class of trouble and both mean ZERO writes: a named member
does not sit in the folder this request locked (``foreign_folder_member`` — nothing ties a
photograph's folder to its stack's, so the row exists but may not be moved from here), or
the write moved a different number of rows than the request named and the whole transaction
went back (``membership_changed``).

The absorb answers both for the same two reasons, from the other direction (IMGMGR-289): a
LOOSE photograph of another folder may not be moved into this scene, and a photograph that
stopped being loose between the check and the write takes the whole absorb back with it.
StackExtractConflict.title: StackExtractConflict

StackExtractConflictError.description:
The 409 body as it goes on the wire (IMGMGR-278).

Declared on every route that writes MEMBERSHIP — extraction, absorb (IMGMGR-289) and,
since IMGMGR-314, merge, eject and split — about the same two conditions and in the same
shape. ``representative`` declares none, because it writes a pointer and no membership, so
neither condition can arise there and a status code declared on a route that never emits it
would be as wrong as an emitted one nobody declared. The name is the extraction's because
that is where the shape was first published, and renaming a component a generated client
already types would be a contract break for a body that has not changed.
StackExtractConflictError.title: StackExtractConflictError

StackExtractRequest.description:
Take exactly these members out of the scene and into a new one of their own.

The positional split's sibling (IMGMGR-257): a cut at a position cannot describe a scene
the deriver over-grouped, where the frames that do not belong are scattered through it.
The owner's rule for both is one sentence — the action's SUBJECT is what it acts on — so
this takes the selection and nothing around it.

Refused when it would empty either side, exactly as a split is: a selection that is the
whole membership would leave a memberless row behind.
StackExtractRequest.title: StackExtractRequest

StackMemberPage.description:
One page of a stack's MEMBERSHIP — the authoritative answer, not a filtered view.

Every member, including tombstoned ones, in capture order, keyset-paginated, and
UNAFFECTED by the browse filters that were active when the card was rendered. The filtered
view is the stack row's ``matched_count``; conflating the two would make an expanded stack
show fewer photos than its own badge claims.
StackMemberPage.title: StackMemberPage

StackRepresentativeRequest.description: §F(5)'s manual cover choice. ``null`` clears it and returns to the derived chain.
StackRepresentativeRequest.title: StackRepresentativeRequest

StackSplitRequest.description:
Split BEFORE this member: it and every later member form a new stack.

Refused when either side would be left empty — an empty stack is unreachable by
construction, which is what lets the cover resolution promise a non-null representative.
StackSplitRequest.title: StackSplitRequest

StaleMarkRevision.description:
Why a conditional mark write refused, and which submitted ids the caller must re-read.

The whole request was refused and nothing was applied (IMGMGR-117), so this is never a
partial-success report: ``stale_image_ids`` names every submitted id whose revision had
already moved on, not the first one found, because a client retrying after a refusal needs
the whole set it has to re-read rather than one id per round trip.
StaleMarkRevision.title: StaleMarkRevision

StaleMarkRevisionError.description:
The 409 body as it goes on the wire (IMGMGR-177).

FastAPI wraps an ``HTTPException`` detail in ``{"detail": ...}``, so the declared shape has
to carry that envelope or the generated client would type the refusal one level too
shallow. Like :class:`MaintenanceBusyError`, which this mirrors exactly, it exists to be
DECLARED and not returned: ``app.api.marks._refuse_if_stale`` raises the exception, and
this says what the exception becomes. The two are held together by
``tests/test_api_marks_conditional.py``, which validates the LIVE body against this model
rather than trusting the declaration.
StaleMarkRevisionError.title: StaleMarkRevisionError

StemLookupRequest.description:
A body rather than a query string: stems are filenames, i.e. user data, and the access
log writes a query string verbatim.
StemLookupRequest.title: StemLookupRequest

StoreMountHealth.description:
One store's mount state, three-valued like the old singular tier banner but now PER
store: ``unknown`` = the loop has not probed this store yet (never a false alarm on
boot), ``mounted`` = the last live probe found the store's root and it passed the tier
identity gate, ``absent`` = the probe ran and it did not (gone, unreadable, or the
probe itself errored). Two stores on one surface need to say 'local mounted, archive
absent' at once, which a single boolean cannot. Whether a store has been INDEXED is a
different question and is answered on its own axis, by ``indexed``.
StoreMountHealth.title: StoreMountHealth

SyncReportOut.description:
A projection of the stored run report: counts only. The stored ``report`` is jsonb the
executor writes and may carry paths, so nothing crosses the wire unvalidated.
SyncReportOut.title: SyncReportOut

SyncRequestCreate.description:
``folder_id`` is a REQUIRED key: an explicit ``null`` is the whole library, and a client
that forgets the key must not get a whole-library run. Only JSON ``true`` confirms.
SyncRequestCreate.title: SyncRequestCreate

SyncRequestOut.description:
One sync request as clients see it. ``requested_iss`` and the executor's host/pid are
operator data and are not exposed.
SyncRequestOut.title: SyncRequestOut

UploadBatchReport.description:
The result report: how many of the batch's files are in each state. Named fields
rather than a map, so a state is part of the contract and never a free string.
UploadBatchReport.title: UploadBatchReport

UploadBearerRefusalError.description:
The 403 every upload route answers a device token with: these routes are the
browser's, behind the edge's forward-auth, and a PAT is never an uploader.
UploadBearerRefusalError.title: UploadBearerRefusalError

UploadBusyError.description:
503: every upload slot is streaming. Nothing changed; ``Retry-After`` says when to
try again. Never a wait — a parked request would hold a connection the page needs.
UploadBusyError.title: UploadBusyError

UploadConflictError.description: 409 on the date control of a sealed batch: its plan is the importer's input now.
UploadConflictError.title: UploadConflictError

client_lastmodified_ms.description: The card file's modification time, epoch milliseconds UTC, within years 0001-9999; outside that range the whole manifest is refused (422 invalid_request) and nothing is recorded.
client_lastmodified_ms.title: Client Lastmodified Ms

UploadManifestFile.description:
One manifest entry's answer, at the entry's own ``position``. A refused entry repeats
neither its client id nor its name — the value refused may be path-shaped — and carries
only the rule it broke.
UploadManifestFile.title: UploadManifestFile

UploadPrecheck.description:
A bandwidth hint, never a verdict: the library holds a file with this name, this size
and this capture day. The client MAY skip sending it (listing it as suppressed, with an
"upload anyway"); the server records nothing about it and claims nothing about content.
UploadPrecheck.title: UploadPrecheck

UploadRefusal.description: Why an upload request was refused, coded. Nothing was staged by it.
UploadRefusal.title: UploadRefusal

UploadRefusalError.description: The coded 422 body as it goes on the wire — the :class:`LookRefusalError` idiom.
UploadRefusalError.title: UploadRefusalError

UploadSeal.description:
The seal's optional body. ``skipped`` names the files the uploader chose not to send
because the pre-check called them likely duplicates; each must still be ``queued`` and
carry that verdict, or the seal is refused ``skip_not_allowed``. Empty or absent: nothing
is skipped, and every file must have been sent or withdrawn.
UploadSeal.title: UploadSeal

bearerAuth.description: A personal access token (`imgmgr_pat_...`), minted by the native device login handoff (`POST /api/auth/native/exchange`) or, for a sibling service, the `mint-service-pat` command. Accepted only on `/api/auth/native/renew`, `/api/auth/native/logout` and `/api/lookup/stems` — every other route stays edge-authenticated (Traefik + Authelia) and reads no Bearer claim, except that `POST /api/sync` records a presented token's subject as the requester (the two sync reads record nothing).

post.description:
Trade a handoff code plus its PKCE verifier for a device PAT.

Anonymous by construction — this is how a device gets its first credential at all, so
requiring one would be circular. Every failure is a 400 with a stable, machine-
readable ``detail``, and every one of them is terminal: the code is burned by the
attempt whatever its outcome, so the client starts a new login rather than retrying.
Revoke the presenting device token, and only that one.

Rotate the presenting device token: mint a successor and revoke the presenter,

post.description:
Take LOOSE photographs into an existing scene — the eject's inverse (IMGMGR-289).

The gesture the family was missing. Merge joins two SCENES, and every other editor starts
from a membership, so a photograph that belonged to no scene had no way into one: eject had
no inverse. This starts from the stream instead, and it is the ONLY editor whose subject is
a photograph that is not already a member.

**The ids are physical.** Exactly the identity merge, eject, split and extract name — an
``Image.id``, resolved to no canonical twin anywhere on this route. An archive photograph's
local mirror is a different row here, and the reader who pointed at one of them gets that
one. Duplicates are removed first, so a body naming the same photograph twice asks for one
row to move; the deduped count is what the rowcount fence below is held against.

**Loose means loose, the target included.** A member of ANY scene is refused — moving a
photograph between scenes is a different operation, and doing it silently would take it out
of one the reader never named. Refusing the target's OWN members is what makes the request
idempotent in the only way it can be: absorbing the same photograph twice is refused the
second time. A tombstone is refused under its own code: it satisfies ``stack_id IS NULL``
like any loose row, and absorbed it would join a scene it cannot be seen in.

**Nothing is written about order or cover.** There is no position column and no cover
column: the membership is served in capture order and the cover is resolved from the
members' current state on every read (``app.stacks.representative``). So a photograph
absorbed from before the scene's first frame takes its chronological place in the band, and
— an unpicked scene being covered by its earliest member — may take the card with it,
without this handler electing anything. What it does write is the anchor, because that IS a
stored column and the browse orders on it.

``_drop_stale_override`` is deliberately not called: an absorb only ADDS members, so a cover
choice that pointed at a member of this scene still points at a member of this scene.

put.description:
One file's bytes, as the raw request body (``application/octet-stream``).

Refused before a byte is written when the batch is sealed, the file is not waiting for
bytes, its size is above the per-file cap, or app data has less free space than the floor.
The body is hashed SHA-256 + md5 + xxh64 in one pass as it streams, aborted at the first
byte past the declared size, and refused if short or if its SHA-256 is not the declared
one — in each case the partial file is deleted and the row records why. A verified file is
then admitted by content: bytes already in the library are ``skipped_duplicate`` with the
path that holds them, and are not kept.

post.description:
Seal the batch: the promise that it is complete, and the importer's input from here.

The optional body lists the files the uploader chose NOT to send (``skipped``): each must
be in this batch, still ``queued``, and have been called a likely duplicate by the
manifest's pre-check — otherwise the seal is refused ``skip_not_allowed``. Listed files
become ``skipped`` in the same commit as the seal; nothing on disk is touched. The skip is
the uploader's decision alone: the seal never consults the pre-check itself, so an empty
or absent list ("upload anyway") skips nothing. Any other file still waiting for or
receiving bytes refuses the seal ``files_outstanding`` — send or withdraw it first. The
whole batch is re-planned under the seal, so every admitted file carries its final plan.

The seal is committed FIRST; only then is the ready marker written, at
``uploads/ready/<batch>``. The ledger is the durable record of outstanding work and the
marker only a wake-up hint, so a marker that cannot be written is logged and the batch is
left for the importer's reconciling timer; it is still sealed.
